text:
Maya (CEO): dropping the Q&A thread for folks who missed the all-hands segment on customer wins/losses. please post clarifying questions here.
Liam (Head of Sales): quick note: a couple of recent losses cited price vs self-hosted quantized setups; a few wins cited reliability and help with evals.
Elena (Customer Success): +1. the assisted eval play closed 3 pilots last quarter. customers keep saying 'help us score outputs' matters more than raw specs.
Sam P. (VP Product): curious: for the reliability wins, was it feature parity or operational setup (e.g., pre-warming)?
Rohit (Solutions Eng): (joining) operational setup: pinned pools + KV pre-warm and a small concurrency bump during demo windows. reduced tail spikes.
Anya (PM): product ask: should we add "pre-warm" presets in Dedicated UI? simple presets: balanced / latency-first / cost-first.
Maya (CEO): yes to presets. surface tradeoffs clearly. also we should start documenting the eval assistance offering as a negotiable add-on.
Liam (Head of Sales): can we commit to a standard scope for evals? Sales loses deals when scope is vague.
DeployBot: _note_: infra/playbooks/eval-onboarding.md created by Anya at 2176543228 :white_check_mark:
Anya (PM): I'll draft a 1-pager for Sales + CS: includes preset configs, sample route_policy snippet, and recommended batch/cache hints. draft by Tue.
Sam P. (VP Product): small roadmap tweak: bump pre-warm UX and an early-console telemetry card that explains tail spikes to customers.
Maya (CEO): great. action items: Anya drafts materials; Legal to sign off on eval add-on wording; Sales to share anonymized RFP notes with Product. follow-ups in leadership sync next week.
